criteria.text: The memo identifies that Corvane's proposed acquisition of 100% of Halvorsen's membership interests under the LOI is a change of control. It must state that Section 14.2 of the distribution agreement treats this as an assignment requiring Brightwater's prior written consent, and that failure to obtain consent lets Brightwater terminate. It must also state that the LOI's Conditions to Closing (Section 6) do not include obtaining that consent. It must recommend obtaining Brightwater's consent before closing and/or adding it as a closing condition.

The memo identifies that Section 3.1 of Amendment No. 1 uses "Products" to mean all goods offered by Supplier, including spare parts and accessories. It must state that this is inconsistent with the Agreement's Section 1.1 definition, which covers only the espresso machines in Exhibit A. It must explain that the amendment controls under the order-of-precedence clause (Section 19.2). It must explain that the minimum purchase commitment and the exclusive distribution rights therefore cover different product scopes. It must recommend a corrective or conforming amendment.

The memo identifies that the renewal notice dated October 15, 2026 was sent after the deadline under Section 2.2 of the distribution agreement. That deadline is written notice at least 90 days before the Initial Term expires on December 31, 2026, i.e., by about October 2, 2026. The memo must explain that the renewal option has likely lapsed or is at risk. It must recommend seeking Brightwater's written agreement to renew or a waiver.
The memo states that the annual minimum purchase commitment under Amendment No. 1 is $2,400,000.
The memo states that the Initial Term of the distribution agreement expires on December 31, 2026.
The memo states that the LOI's target closing date is November 30, 2026.
The memo places time-sensitive items at or near the top. These items must include at least the missed renewal deadline or the change of control consent needed before closing.

The memo is addressed to the supervising partner. For each issue it identifies, the memo states the document and section where the issue appears, why it matters for Halvorsen, and a recommended fix or course of action.

The response fails if it flags the Tidemark warehouse services agreement as containing a substantive problem, conflict, or risk requiring action in connection with these issues. Noting that it was reviewed and raises no issue is acceptable.
The response fails if it concludes that the October 15, 2026 renewal notice was timely or that the renewal option was validly exercised.
